title: Cache Hit Attribution and Differential Evals for Output Drift
creator: Leah Chen
description:
Problem: We have observed sporadic semantic drift correlated with cache hits on several model variants. Existing regression checks detect overall output divergence but do not attribute changes to cache hit vs miss paths or quantify whether changes are acceptable. This ticket defines a reproducible attribution and differential-eval pipeline that isolates cache-hit influence on outputs, produces human-reviewable diffs, and gates rollouts when the hit path causes unacceptable quality regressions.

Goal: Build a testable, automated framework that: (1) produces paired hit/miss inference traces for representative prompts, (2) computes fine-grained delta signatures (token diffs, logprob deltas, semantic similarity), (3) attributes output changes to cache-related state (prefix KV differences, warm vs cold attention masks), and (4) surfaces actionable signals for rollouts (fail/pass thresholds, top-k failure examples).
acceptance_criteria: Automated job produces >= 1k paired examples (hit vs miss) for each target model/config per run
Delta signature includes token-level edit distance, normalized logprob delta, and embedding cosine similarity
Attribution heuristic flags likely cache-responsible cases (e.g., only prefix KV differs) with >= 80% precision on manual sample
Blocking rule: any canary release with > 1% critical-question regression (semantic similarity < 0.85 on critical prompts) must fail rollout
Dashboard shows daily trend of hit-induced regressions and surfaces top 50 failure traces for review
Integration tests cover warm/cold path determinism and reproduce a documented historical regression
implementation_steps: Design: finalize paired-run protocol (seeded RNG, same model weights, one run with cache enabled + warmed, one with cache disabled or flushed)
Instrumentation: add deterministic tracing to runtime to record KV signatures, attention masks, and per-token logprobs in both runs
Dataset: assemble representative prompt sets (critical prompts, long-context conversational prompts, code-gen snippets) and subsample stratified by token length
Eval harness: implement differential scoring pipeline that outputs edit diffs, logprob deltas, embedding cosines, and categorizes drift types (prefixal, completion, hallucination)
Attribution heuristics: rule-based and lightweight classifier to mark traces as cache-likely; create manual annotation UI for labeling samples
Integration: wire results into Console dashboard and create a canary gating webhook used by rollout service
Automation: create a scheduled job and on-change trigger (model/config PR) that runs the harness and publishes results
Docs: write runbook for interpreting signals and steps for rollback/mitigation (cache flush, pin older quantization, restrict batching)
eval_harness_spec: Paired execution: for each prompt, run A: cold (cache cleared) and B: warmed (replay warm path) with identical RNG and system env
Trace capture: include input prompt hash, prefix KV fingerprint, per-layer KV counters, per-token logprobs, sampling seed, latency, and node id
Delta metrics: token_edit_distance, normalized_logprob_delta (sum per token / token_count), embedding_cosine_on_completion, top_k_token_change_rate
Categorization: prefix-confined (differences confined to first N tokens after prefix), downstream-drift (differences appear later), confidence-collapse (logprob drop > threshold)
Sampling rules: stratify by context length bins [<128, 128-512, 512-2048, >2048] and by prompt type [instruction, chat, code, multi-turn]
metrics: hit_regression_rate (fraction of paired traces where embedding_cosine < 0.9 AND token_edit_distance > 2)
rollout_plan: Pre-merge: run harness on candidate model/config in CI; require generated report artifact
Canary: deploy to 1% traffic with gating webhook; if hit_regression_rate > configured threshold, abort and auto-roll back
Post-rollout: daily monitor for 7 days; auto-create incident if trend slope for hit_regression_rate > 0.2%/day
Mitigations: automatic cache flush, revert batching config, fall back to compatible model variant with earlier KV semantics
